Copilot is launched WITHOUT --allow-all (COPILOT_NO_ALLOW_ALL=1) — with it, every call is pre-approved and the fixture would be a duplicate of 2-2 auto-executed-tool-call. Confirmed in this recording: the bash call produced tool.execution_start + tool.execution_complete and NO permission.requested line anywhere, and no session.permissions_changed turned allowAllPermissions on. The risky branch is 2-19 tool-gate-permission-prompt; like the claudecode sibling, one recipe cannot both hold in waiting and settle to ready.

VACUITY WARNING WITHDRAWN 2026-08-03 (re-recorded after the fix). The earlier recording of this cell carried a vacuity caveat: while session.MergeMetrics dropped TranscriptPermissionPending, NO copilot session could reach waiting from the transcript at all, so the no-waiting invariant passed for a reason unrelated to the agent's classifier. That bug is fixed (commit "fix(session): carry TranscriptPermissionPending through MergeMetrics") and the sibling cell 2-19 tool-gate-permission-prompt was re-recorded green on the SAME daemon build, live-emitting state_transition new_state=waiting reason "transcript permission prompt open → waiting". The waiting machinery is therefore demonstrably live, and this cell's no-waiting invariant now discriminates for the RIGHT reason: the read-only shell call was classified safe by the agent and raised no permission.requested.

BIRTH SHAPE: the real session is born DIRECTLY into working, not ready. copilot creates session-state/<id>/ at launch holding only workspace.yaml and writes events.jsonl only when the first prompt is sent, so the open turn is already on disk at discovery and the birth is classified against its own metrics. The transient proc-<PID> row is still born ready and remains the presession anchor; session_birth and turn_start are ONE phase.

PHASE SHAPE: Copilot writes TWO assistant.turn_end events per tool-using prompt, each mapping to turn_done → ready, so a brief mid-prompt ready blip is possible; the no-waiting invariant is therefore carried by a `kind`-anchored phase whose duration_at_least_ms bounds only the invariant window (checkDurationAtLeast is skipped when expected_state is empty), not by a long-held `working` phase a blip would fail. OBSERVATIONS mirror 2-2: tokens/cost non-zero from assistant.message.outputTokens; model unpinned because --model accepts only 'auto' and the router picks per turn.
